newsitem.title: POLAND: EBRD to buy stake in Polish screw-maker for $4 mln.
newsitem.headline: EBRD to buy stake in Polish screw-maker for $4 mln.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) agreed to take a 33 percent stake in Polish screw-maker Srubena SA for $4 million, Srubena's main shareholder said in a statement.

National Investment Fund (NFI) No. 8, which currently holds 33 percent of Srubena, said the firm would first hold a rights issue of the same size for current shareholders so that the fund remained the largest shareholder.

"The total value of the new share issue will be $8 million with the EBRD to subscribe to $4 million and Octava NFI (No. 8) subscribing to the majority of the remaining $4 million," the statement said.

Srubena, which employes 1,200, now has a capital of 16.96 million zlotys ($5.95 million) divided into 1,580,000 shares. It made a six-million- zloty net loss in the first nine months of this year on sales of 58 million zlotys.
The rights issue will also be adressed to the 14 other NFIs which each hold less than two percent of the firm, to employees and to the state treasury, which has 20 percent. @
Cash from the issues, which must be approved by a Srubena shareholders meeting on December 12, would be used to help finance the firm's planned investment of $10 million by 1999.
The statement said that Srubena, located in the southern town of Zywiec, would be a "good candidate for the Warsaw Stock Exchange in a few years time."
